Request

paragraphs.html:
The Hon. Matthew Guy MP, Leader of the Liberals and
Nationals, requested that I undertake an independent assessment of the financial
impact of the parties’ election platform. The Liberals and Nationals’ platform
consists of:
paragraphs.text: The Hon. Matthew Guy MP, Leader of the Liberals and Nationals, requested that I undertake an independent assessment of the financial impact of the parties’ election platform. The Liberals and Nationals’ platform consists of:

listItems.html: §  94 aggregated groups of election policies (election policies) listed in the ‘Individual election policy impacts’ section of this report
listItems.text: 94 aggregated groups of election policies (election policies) listed in the ‘Individual election policy impacts’ section of this report

listItems.html: §  18 additional election policies included in an attachment to this report – we expect that none of these would have a financial impact on the state budget.
listItems.text: 18 additional election policies included in an attachment to this report – we expect that none of these would have a financial impact on the state budget.

paragraphs.html:
The Leader advised me that this report, including an
attachment of election policy summaries, represent all the Liberals and
Nationals’ election policies they would enact should they form government after
the 2022 Victorian election. It replaces all commitments made since the
commencement of the election period on 3 May 2022. In the absence of
commitments made after the release of this report, I agree that it is a full
reflection of the Liberals and Nationals’ election policy platform.
paragraphs.text: The Leader advised me that this report, including an attachment of election policy summaries, represent all the Liberals and Nationals’ election policies they would enact should they form government after the 2022 Victorian election. It replaces all commitments made since the commencement of the election period on 3 May 2022. In the absence of commitments made after the release of this report, I agree that it is a full reflection of the Liberals and Nationals’ election policy platform.

paragraphs.html:
I was given sufficient policy detail to enable me to examine
each of these election policies and make judgements. In preparing my
assessment, I used my own calculations, approach and assumptions, supported by
legislated access to Victorian public sector information.
paragraphs.text: I was given sufficient policy detail to enable me to examine each of these election policies and make judgements. In preparing my assessment, I used my own calculations, approach and assumptions, supported by legislated access to Victorian public sector information.
Response

paragraphs.html:
Compared to the 2022 Victorian Pre-Election Budget Update
released on 10 November 2022, this report shows how I expect these election policies
would change the overall budget position and finances of the state. It also
shows how each individual election policy would change the budget if implemented.
To aid understanding, the election policies are categorised by the Liberals and
Nationals into policy bundles – a classification of the parties’ policy
objectives.
paragraphs.text: Compared to the 2022 Victorian Pre-Election Budget Update released on 10 November 2022, this report shows how I expect these election policies would change the overall budget position and finances of the state. It also shows how each individual election policy would change the budget if implemented. To aid understanding, the election policies are categorised by the Liberals and Nationals into policy bundles – a classification of the parties’ policy objectives.

GAICD FCPA Fellow ANZSOG
Parliamentary Budget Officer of Victoria
24 November 2022
Budget position

paragraphs.html:
We assessed how the Liberals and Nationals’ election
policies would impact Victoria’s budget position for the period corresponding
with the 2022 Victorian Pre-Election Budget Update (to 2025–26) and over the
next parliament (to 2026–27) where possible – as budget aggregates, like net
debt, only exist to 2025–26.
paragraphs.text: We assessed how the Liberals and Nationals’ election policies would impact Victoria’s budget position for the period corresponding with the 2022 Victorian Pre-Election Budget Update (to 2025–26) and over the next parliament (to 2026–27) where possible – as budget aggregates, like net debt, only exist to 2025–26.

tableRows.html: On 30 June 2026, these election policies would decrease net debt to $155.6 billion, which is $10.4 billion lower than the budget.
tableRows.text: On 30 June 2026, these election policies would decrease net debt to $155.6 billion, which is $10.4 billion lower than the budget.

tableRows.html: In 2025–26, the net operating balance would be $11.3 billion, which is $10.5 billion higher than the budget.
tableRows.text: In 2025–26, the net operating balance would be $11.3 billion, which is $10.5 billion higher than the budget.
Net debt as a share of the economy

tableRows.html: On 30 June 2026, these election policies would decrease net debt as a share of nominal gross state product (GSP) to 23.1% which is 1.5 percentage points lower than the budget.
tableRows.text: On 30 June 2026, these election policies would decrease net debt as a share of nominal gross state product (GSP) to 23.1% which is 1.5 percentage points lower than the budget.

paragraphs.text: Budget impact by policy bundle

paragraphs.html:
The change in net position indicates the overall impact of
these election policies on the Victorian budget. It is similar to a change in
net debt and measures the gap between the government’s operating revenue and
expenses, and movements in assets. A positive change indicates that these
election policies would improve the net position of the budget.
paragraphs.text: The change in net position indicates the overall impact of these election policies on the Victorian budget. It is similar to a change in net debt and measures the gap between the government’s operating revenue and expenses, and movements in assets. A positive change indicates that these election policies would improve the net position of the budget.

paragraphs.html:
We estimated how these election policies would change the 2022
Victorian Pre-Election Budget Update to 2026–27, by the Liberals and Nationals’
policy bundles.
paragraphs.text: We estimated how these election policies would change the 2022 Victorian Pre-Election Budget Update to 2026–27, by the Liberals and Nationals’ policy bundles.
Change in asset investment

paragraphs.html:
Compared to the 2022 Victorian Pre-Election Budget Update,
we expect that these election policies would increase total estimated
investment by $5,492.5 million over their project lifecycles.
paragraphs.text: Compared to the 2022 Victorian Pre-Election Budget Update, we expect that these election policies would increase total estimated investment by $5,492.5 million over their project lifecycles.
Budget impact of Shelve the Suburban Rail Loop to fund health

paragraphs.html: We estimate that ‘Shelve the Suburban Rail Loop to fund health’ would increase the state’s budgeted net position by $10,248.6 million. When offset against ‘Hospital capital package’, ‘Health growth fund’ and ‘Halve elective surgery wait lists’, there would be a residual increase to the state’s budgeted net position of $3,111.6 million between 2022–23 and 2032–33.
paragraphs.text: We estimate that ‘Shelve the Suburban Rail Loop to fund health’ would increase the state’s budgeted net position by $10,248.6 million.
